title: Changelog
text: FindAbundantMarkers keep markers whose CPM exceeds isotype-relative ratio /absolute abundance threshold least min_cell_fraction cells. CPM uses per-marker pseudocount 1 ((x + 1) / sum(x + 1) * 1e6). return_stats = TRUE, marker, including isotype controls, includes median_cpm CPM range visible choosing abundance_threshold. Added PixelDB$components_cell_graph() method directly extract bipartite cell graphs associated marker counts DuckDB edgelists using 64-bit integer hashing (bit64), achieving faster graph instantiation lower peak memory usage. ComputeLayout() method CellGraphList objects, layouts can computed directly list returned CellGraphs(). Unloaded (NULL) graphs kept place result CellGraphList.

title: Skill: Generate Unit Tests for pixelatorR
text: Every test file follows three-part layout:
code: # ── 1. Setup: Load data ────────────────────────────────── library(dplyr) pxl_file <- minimal_pna_pxl_file() prox <- ReadPNA_proximity(pxl_file)  # ── 2. Tests: Expected behavior ────────────────────────── test_that("<function_name> works as expected", {   expect_no_error(result <- <function_name>(...))   # Prefer data-level assertions (see "Assertion Preferences" below)   expect_equal(result[1:5, 1:3], <expected_snippet>) })  # ── 3. Tests: Invalid input ────────────────────────────── test_that("<function_name> fails with invalid input", {   expect_error(<function_name>("Invalid"))   expect_error(<function_name>(data, bad_param = "Invalid")) })

title: Skill: Generate Unit Tests for pixelatorR
text: full example ColocalizationHeatmap:
code: library(dplyr) prox <- ReadPNA_proximity(minimal_pna_pxl_file()) prox_summarized <- prox %>%   slice_sample(n = 1e4) %>%   group_by(marker_1, marker_2) %>%   summarize(mean_log2_ratio = mean(log2_ratio), .groups = "drop") %>%   mutate(test1 = marker_1, test2 = marker_2, estimate = mean_log2_ratio) %>%   ungroup()  test_that("ColocalizationHeatmap works as expected", {   # Default method   expect_no_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized))    # Dots method   expect_no_error(p <- ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, type = "dots",                                               size_col = "mean_log2_ratio"))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_1))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_2))   expect_equal(p$data$marker_1 %>% levels(), p$data$marker_2 %>% levels())    # Custom marker columns   expect_no_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized,                                          marker1_col = "test1",                                          marker2_col = "test2"))    # Custom value column   expect_no_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized,                                          value_col = "mean_log2_ratio"))    # Symmetrise FALSE   expect_no_error(p <- ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, symmetrise = FALSE,                                               type = "dots",                                               size_col = "mean_log2_ratio"))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_1))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_2))   expect_true(!identical(p$data$marker_1 %>% levels(),                          p$data$marker_2 %>% levels())) })  test_that("ColocalizationHeatmap fails with invalid input", {   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap("Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, marker1_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, marker2_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, value_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, type = "dots",                                       size_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized,                                       size_col_transform = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, size_range = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, colors = FALSE))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, cluster_rows = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, cluster_cols = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, type = "Invalid")) })

title: Introduction
text: Seurat v5, new Assay type introduced called Assay5. Users can switch using Assay Assay5 classes store counts data setting global option Seurat.object.assay.version either “v3” “v5”. Similarly, pixelatorR, can set global option control whether use CellGraphAssay/PNAAssay CellGraphAssay5/PNAAssay5 class. CellGraphAssay/PNAAssay classes extend Assay class CellGraphAssay5/PNAAssay5 class extend Assay5 class, providing additional slots store spatial metrics component graphs.

title: Load data
text: Perhaps useful function ReadMPX_Seurat allows us load MPX data Seurat object additional bells whistles provided pixelatorR. , options modify Seurat created. First foremost, can set return_cellgraphassay = FALSE return Seurat object includes abundance measurements. simpler data set, count matrix stored Assay without spatial data. means almost information unique MPX ignored able analyze visualize graphs way explore spatial statistics. However, basic data set uses significantly less memory faster process can useful protein abundance interesting data type analysis. default, ReadMPX_Seurat returns MPX data object called CellGraphAssay. object class extends Assay class Seurat essentially Assay object additional data slots. CellGraphAssay class covered detail later tutorial. additional parameters ReadMPX_Seurat controls behavior return_cellgraphassay = TRUE. default, MPX polarization scores colocalization scores loaded stored CellGraphAssay named “mpxCells”.
code: seur_obj <- ReadMPX_Seurat(pxl_file) # Load simpler data set seur_obj <- ReadMPX_Seurat(pxl_file, return_cellgraphassay = FALSE) ## Warning: Data is of class matrix. Coercing to dgCMatrix. seur_obj[["mpxCells"]] ## Assay (v5) data with 80 features for 477 cells ## Top 10 variable features: ##  CD274, CD44, CD25, CD279, CD41, HLA-ABC, CD54, CD26, CD27, CD38  ## Layers: ##  counts seur_obj <- ReadMPX_Seurat(pxl_file) seur_obj ## An object of class Seurat  ## 80 features across 477 samples within 1 assay  ## Active assay: mpxCells (80 features, 80 variable features) ##  1 layer present: counts

title: Calculate dispersion of components — CalculateDispersion
text: Calculate dispersion numeric data Seurat object matrix. dispersion calculated summary statistic distribution values (counts) across components. dispersion can calculated using Gini coefficient Tau statistic. Gini Tau coefficients measures inequality distribution, ranging 0 1, 0 signifies perfectly equal distribution 1 signifies perfectly unequal distribution. terms marker counts across different markers component, low dispersion indicates marker counts similar levels across markers, high dispersion indicates marker counts distributed mostly one markers. dispersion can example used quantitative metric assess whether component's counts dispersed markers expected level. high low dispersion can indicate component kind artifact, rather real cell.

text: cellgraph tbl_graph object corresponding cell graph nodes Character vector node IDs graph order. map used align counts, layouts, layers, metadata, reductions. tables stored order without copying IDs row names. counts matrix-like object marker counts (nodes x markers). Rows follow nodes. counts matrix can extracted "counts" layer via Layers / LayerData. layout named list data.frame objects coordinates cell layouts. Rows follow nodes. name column explicit row names accepted input used reorder; MPX bipartite layouts may omit -/-B suffixes. Stored layouts keep coordinate columns (typically x, y, z). Layouts without node IDs still work number rows matches graph. layers named list additional numeric node matrices (nodes x features), analogous layers Seurat Assay5. layer can extracted via Layers / LayerData. meta.data data.frame node-level metadata (one row per node). A tibble: 45 × 4 #>    marker_1 marker_2 estimate      p_adj #>    <chr>    <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> #>  1 M2       M1        -0.560  0.176      #>  2 M2       M10       -0.230  0.00639    #>  3 M3       M1         1.56   0.00858    #>  4 M3       M2         0.0705 0.0000275  #>  5 M3       M10        0.129  0.00147    #>  6 M4       M1         1.72   0.000311   #>  7 M4       M2         0.461  0.00114    #>  8 M4       M3        -1.27   0.00122    #>  9 M4       M10       -0.687  0.00000183 #> 10 M5       M1        -0.446  0.00283    #> # ℹ 35 more rows  # Typical heatmap ColocalizationHeatmap(dca_markers)   # Skip symmetrisation ColocalizationHeatmap(dca_markers, symmetrise = FALSE)   # Typical dot plot # Note that the size legend title needs to be set manually ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers,   type = "dots",   size_range = c(1, 10),   size_col_transform = \(x) {     -log10(x)   } ) &   labs(size = "-log10p(p_adj)")   # Outline selected marker pairs (constant colour) ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers,   type = "dots",   size_range = c(1, 10),   highlight_pairs = tibble(     marker_1 = c("M1", "M3"),     marker_2 = c("M2", "M5")   ),   highlight_colors = "black" )   # Map border colours from a column in highlight_pairs (dots only) ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers,   type = "dots",   size_range = c(1, 10),   highlight_pairs = tibble(     marker_1 = c("M1", "M3"),     marker_2 = c("M2", "M5"),     database = c("string", "alphafold")   ),   highlight_color_col = "database",   highlight_colors = c(string = "#C0392B", alphafold = "#6C3483"),   highlight_shrink = 0.15 )   # We can specify the order of the markers with factor levels # but we need to turn off the clustering ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers %>%     mutate(       marker_1 = factor(marker_1, levels = paste0("M", 1:10)),       marker_2 = factor(marker_2, levels = paste0("M", 1:10))     ),   type = "dots",   size_range = c(1, 10),   size_col_transform = \(x) {     -log10(x)   },   cluster_rows = FALSE,   cluster_cols = FALSE ) &   labs(size = "-log10p(p_adj)")   # If there are multiple comparisons per marker pair, we need to subset # the data first dca_markers_two_tests <- bind_rows(   dca_markers %>% mutate(refrence = "ctrl", target = "stim1"),   dca_markers %>% mutate(refrence = "ctrl", target = "stim2") ) dca_markers_two_tests #> # A tibble: 90 × 6 #>    marker_1 marker_2 estimate      p_adj refrence target #>    <chr>    <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>    <chr>  #>  1 M2       M1        -0.560  0.176      ctrl     stim1  #>  2 M2       M10       -0.230  0.00639    ctrl     stim1  #>  3 M3       M1         1.56   0.00858    ctrl     stim1  #>  4 M3       M2         0.0705 0.0000275  ctrl     stim1  #>  5 M3       M10        0.129  0.00147    ctrl     stim1  #>  6 M4       M1         1.72   0.000311   ctrl     stim1  #>  7 M4       M2         0.461  0.00114    ctrl     stim1  #>  8 M4       M3        -1.27   0.00122    ctrl     stim1  #>  9 M4       M10       -0.687  0.00000183 ctrl     stim1  #> 10 M5       M1        -0.446  0.00283    ctrl     stim1  #> # ℹ 80 more rows  # This will now fail if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ColocalizationHeatmap(dca_markers_two_tests) } # }  # We need to subset the data first ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers_two_tests %>%     filter(target == "stim1") )

text: Takes object colocalization scores long format returns object colocalization scores wide format. colocalization score table includes various colocalization scores along p-values pair markers component. wide format array-like object dimensions (markers_1 * marker_2) x components, cell filled polarization score. title: Compute proximity scores — ComputeProximityScores
text: mean standard deviations calculated either permutations using analytical formulas. See details . Finally, two proximity metrics computed resulting join_count statistics.

title: Compute proximity scores — ComputeProximityScores
text: expected mean calculated \(p_{umi1,m1} * p_{umi2,m2} * S0\), \(p_{umi1,m1}\) \(p_{umi2,m2}\)  frequencies two markers graph umi1 umi2 nodes, respectively. \(S0\) total number edges graph. formula variance join count statistic given (eq. 8, Epperson, B. K. 2002): $$ Var_{m1m2} = \frac{1}{4} \times (2S1p_{umi1,m1}p_{umi2,m2} + (S2 - 2S1)(p_{umi1,m1}p_{umi2,m2}(p_{umi1,m1} + p_{umi2,m2})) + 4(S1 - S2)(p_{umi1,m1}^2p_{umi2,m2}^2)) $$ $$ S1 = \frac{1}{2} \times (\sum_{,j} (A_{ij} + A_{ji})^2) $$ $$ S2 = \sum_{} \left(\sum_{j} (A_{ij} + A_{ji})^2\right) $$

title: PXL database class — PixelDB
text: class provides interface working PXL file. PXL file duckdb database contains various tables created Pixelator data processing pipeline. class provides methods query database extract information . class intended used internally package exposed user advanced use cases. Example usage:
code: # Create a PixelDB object with a connection to a PXL file pxl_db <- PixelDB$new("path/to/pxl/file") pxl_db$info()  # Fetch count matrix counts <- pxl_db$counts()  # Fetch proximity scores proximity <- pxl_db$proximity()

title: Convert proximity score table to an Assay or Assay5 — ProximityScoresToAssay
text: object object proximity scores ... yet implemented values_from single string defining column proximity score table pick values . Default "log2_ratio". separator character separate marker names row names output. Default ":". Must single character must appear marker name. lazy Whether look proximity scores PXL file instead Assay / Assay5 object. assay Name PNAAssay PNAAssay5 pull proximity scores new_assay Name Assay Assay5 store wide formatted spatial metric

title: Convert proximity score table to an Assay or Assay5 — ProximityScoresToAssay
text: Takes object PNA proximity scores long format returns object proximity scores wide format. proximity score table must contain following columns: "marker_1": name first marker pair "marker_2": name second marker pair "component": name component column proximity scores used values wide format (defined values_from parameter) wide format array-like object dimensions pair x components, pair defined combination "marker_1" "marker_2" separated separator, element array filled value selected spatial metric. Note observations missing proximity score table replaced 0's. Proximity scores can also 0 (deviation random expectations), possible distinguish two cases output. Different outputs returned depending input object type: tibble/data.frame: returns dgCMatrix marker pairs rows components columns. components ordered particular way therefore ordered placing e.g. Seurat object. PNAAssay/PNAAssay5: returns Assay Assay5 marker pairs rows components columns. Columns ordered according order components PNAAssay/PNAAssay5. Seurat object: returns Seurat object new Assay Assay5 marker pairs rows components columns. Columns ordered according order components Seurat object. many methods provided Seurat operates Assay/Assay5 objects, can sometimes convenient make conversion wish use methods spatial metrics proximity score table. instance, want compute UMAP proximity scores RunUMAP, need values formatted Assay/Assay5. also makes possible use various visualization functions VlnPlot FeaturePlot show distribution proximity scores.

title: Restore PXL file paths — RestorePaths
text: typical situation function useful export Seurat object created pixelatorR RDS file, share someone else. ensure data available recipient, also need share raw PXL files make sure recipient updates PXL file paths Seurat object RestorePaths. instance, assume Seurat object seurat_obj created pixelatorR PXL files stored directory DATA_DIR local system. can export Seurat object RDS file : content DATA_DIR might look like : Now can share entire DATA_DIR folder someone else. recipient loads RDS file R, PXL file paths Seurat object need updated, recipients DATA_DIR different . Assuming recipient stored PXL file RDS object directory RECIPIENT_DATA_DIR, recipient can update PXL file paths :
code: saveRDS(seurat_obj, file = file.path(DATA_DIR, "seurat_obj.rds")) DATA_DIR ├── seurat_obj.rds └── Sample01_pbmc.analysis.pxl seurat_obj <- readRDS(file = file.path(RECIPIENT_DATA_DIR, "seurat_obj.rds")) seurat_obj <- RestorePaths(seurat_obj, pxl_files_dir = RECIPIENT_DATA_DIR)

title: Restore PXL file paths — RestorePaths
code: library(pixelatorR) library(dplyr)  # Load example data as a Seurat object pxl_file <- minimal_mpx_pxl_file()  # Copy PXL file to tempdir tmp_pxl_file <- file.path(fs::path_temp(), "five_cells.pxl") fs::file_copy(pxl_file, tmp_pxl_file) seur_obj <- ReadMPX_Seurat(tmp_pxl_file) #> ✔ Created a 'Seurat' object with 5 cells and 80 targeted surface proteins  # Now we can load graphs seur_obj <- LoadCellGraphs(seur_obj, cells = colnames(seur_obj)[1]) #> →    Loading CellGraphs for 1 cells from sample 1 #> ✔ Successfully loaded 1 CellGraph object(s).  # Removing or moving PXL file will make graphs inaccessible fs::file_delete(tmp_pxl_file) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # This will now fail since the PXL file is missing seur_obj <- LoadCellGraphs(seur_obj, force = TRUE) } # }  # We can restore paths to the PXL file using RestorePaths. # All we need is to provide the path to a directory where the PXL file is located. pxl_files_dir <- system.file("extdata/five_cells",   package = "pixelatorR" ) seur_obj <- RestorePaths(seur_obj, pxl_files_dir = pxl_files_dir) #> ✔ Successfully updated PXL file paths.  # Now LoadCellGraphs should work as expected seur_obj <- LoadCellGraphs(seur_obj, force = TRUE) #> →    Loading CellGraphs for 5 cells from sample 1 #> ✔ Successfully loaded 5 CellGraph object(s).

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: tibble following columns: component component (cell) identifier. read_count estimated number reads downsampling. p downsampling fraction. nodes estimated number nodes retained. edges estimated number edges retained. degree estimated average node degree. node_saturation node saturation given fraction. edge_saturation edge saturation given fraction.

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: downsampling performed probabilistically using expected values rather actual random sampling. edge given read_count, probability edge retained fraction p : $$P(\text{edge retained}) = 1 - (1 - p)^{\text{read\_count}}$$ nodes, probability retention depends node's degree. node retained least one incident edges retained: $$P(\text{node retained}) = 1 - (1 - p_{edges})^{\text{degree}}$$ \(p_{edges}\) fraction edges retained.

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: saturation values calculated using: $$S = 1 - \frac{N_{downsampled}}{R_{downsampled}}$$ \(N_{downsampled}\) number nodes edges downsampled graph, \(R_{downsampled}\) number reads supporting elements. Since read supports two nodes (one endpoint), \(R_{downsampled, nodes} = 2 \times R_{downsampled, edges}\).

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: function requires approximate_node_saturation called first (either directly function) create nodes temporary view DuckDB connection.

title: Compute heuristic illumination for 3D layouts — heuristic_illumination
code: library(dplyr) set.seed(1)  # Here we simulate some 3D coordinates with a roughly spherical distribution n <- 20000 n_surface <- 19000 n_interior <- 1000  # Surface points: normalize to unit sphere, add small Gaussian noise xyz_surface <- matrix(rnorm(n_surface * 3), ncol = 3) xyz_surface <- xyz_surface / sqrt(rowSums(xyz_surface^2)) # project to unit sphere xyz_surface <- xyz_surface + matrix(rnorm(n_surface * 3, sd = 0.05), ncol = 3)  # Interior points: uniform in ball via rejection sampling xyz_interior <- matrix(rnorm(n_interior * 3), ncol = 3) radii <- runif(n_interior)^(1 / 3) # cube root for uniform volume distribution xyz_interior <- xyz_interior / sqrt(rowSums(xyz_interior^2)) * radii * 0.8  layout <- tibble::tibble(   x = c(xyz_surface[, 1], xyz_interior[, 1]),   y = c(xyz_surface[, 2], xyz_interior[, 2]),   z = c(xyz_surface[, 3], xyz_interior[, 3]) ) illum <- heuristic_illumination(layout)  # Use cell_plot() and cell_plot_animate() to render a rotating layout if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ temp_gif <- fs::file_temp(ext = ".gif") render_rotating_layout(   data = layout %>%     mutate(node_val = illum),   pt_size = 0.8,   width = 740,   height = 650,   colors = PixelgenGradient(100, "NaturalBlue"),   file = temp_gif,   max_degree = 30,   frames = 20,   delay = 1 / 20,   res = 100,   boomerang = TRUE,   show_first_frame = FALSE ) } # }

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) pxl_file <- minimal_pna_pxl_file() components <- ReadPNA_counts(pxl_file) %>% colnames()  # Select fractions based on average read depth db <- PixelDB$new(pxl_file) avg_reads <- db$cell_meta()$reads %>% mean() fracs <- (10^seq(4, log10(avg_reads), length.out = 20))[-20] / avg_reads  lcc_df <- lcc_curve(pxl_file, components, fracs = fracs)  # Plot LCC sizes by fraction ggplot(lcc_df, aes(frac, n_nodes, color = component)) +   geom_point() +   geom_line() +   theme_bw() +   guides(color = "none")  # Compute graph stability (LCC / max theoretical nodes) nodesat <- approximate_node_saturation(db) %>% collect() db$close()  lcc_df <- lcc_df %>%   left_join(nodesat, by = "component")  ggplot(lcc_df, aes(frac, n_nodes / nodes, color = component)) +   geom_point() +   geom_line() +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +   labs(y = "Graph stability (LCC / total nodes)") +   theme_bw() +   guides(color = "none") } # }

text: local proximity statistic defined UMI counts set markers within neighborhood size k around node. statistic comes two flavors depending mode: : "markers must present". : "marker markers can present". neighborhood around node reaches k nearest neighbors, meaning maximum possible distance two nodes neighborhood 2*k edges. observed statistic calculated either: : $$O_{,m} = min(x_{,m})$$ : $$O_{,m} = sum(x_{,m})$$ \(x_{,m}\) vector UMI counts selected markers \(m\) neighborhood node \(\). first mode () default computes minimum UMI count markers neighborhood. used markers need present neighborhood useful identifying colocation entire set (module) markers. second mode () computes sum UMI counts markers neighborhood. useful presence marker sufficient define clustering. instance, want detect region least one markers present. Analytical formula expected value (\(E_{,m}\)) local proximity statistic single node \(\) markers \(m\) given : : $$E_{,m} = min(f_{umi1} \M_{umi1}) \times N_{umi1}() + min(f_{umi2} \M_{umi2}) \times N_{umi2}()$$ : $$E_{,m} = sum(f_{umi1} \M_{umi1}) \times N_{umi1}() + sum(f_{umi2} \M_{umi2}) \times N_{umi2}()$$ \(M_{umi1}\), \(M_{umi2}\) sets marker frequencies selected markers node types umi1 umi2. two node types (umi1/umi2) PNA graph can different marker frequencies therefore treated separately calculation. \(N_{umi1}()\), \(N_{umi2}()\) neighborhood sizes two node types node \(\). local proximity score node \(\) computed : $$LNE_{,m} = log2(\frac{O_{,m}+k-1}{E_{,m}+k-1})$$ \(k-1\) pseudocount used flatten weak signals. higher k result global proximity score, lower k result local proximity score. Hence, k determines "spatial resolution". markers can include number protein IDs: single marker: local clustering Two markers: local proximity Three markers: local proximity multiple markers Note score measures colocation specified markers. Frames drawn x across screen, z screen, y depth, camera's point view +x right, +z , +y toward viewer. default c(-0.6, 0.5, 0.62) places key light viewer's left, slightly front layout (roughly 38 degrees horizon), reads like afternoon sunlight rather flat head-look light camera axis. mask computed , points rotated, key light fixed relative layout rather camera. default direction lit side therefore turns layout full rotation, camera-facing side brightest near start end turn dimmest around halfway point. Pass light_direction = c(0, 0, 1) light along rotation axis instead, keeps apparent shading constant whole rotation.

title: cell:cell conjugate segmentation — segment_cell
text: segment cell:cell conjugates, first need fit NMF model abundance matrix (local node neighborhood abundance profiles) two cell populations using cc_protein_weights function. gives us protein weights cell type (w) can use classification. rule thumb, good NMF model high weights proteins mutually exclusive two cell types. instance, segmenting B cell:T cell conjugate, expect NMF model give high weights CD10, CD20 CD21 B cell identity CD3e, CD2 CD5 T cell identity. membrane segmentation step, create neighborhood profile node summing abundance neighbors graph. project NMF weights (w) onto neighborhood profiles using NNLS get score node cell type.
